basis: Postsynaptic NMJ disorder; muscle fiber damage, atrophy and contractures reported in 1/1 patient. Ophthalmoplegia reflects NMJ weakness rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Oral, dental and digital malformations define the syndrome; strabismus occurs in 2/4 (50%). Speech delay may reflect structural oral abnormalities.
Syndrome defined by neurologic disease, endocrine dysfunction and exocrine pancreatic disease; insufficient cross-subtype evidence for additional organs.
Hereditary tumors of adrenal chromaffin tissue and autonomic paraganglia; hypertension frequency and lasting cardiovascular injury are not established.
HHV-8-associated B-cell lymphoma; malignant pleural and pericardial effusions each annotated 80-99%. Peritoneal occupation also common, omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Recurrent inflammation damages subcutaneous fat. Arthralgia and myalgia do not establish tissue damage; visceral, ocular and autoimmune findings occur in fewer than 30%.
Human respiroviruses cause infection of respiratory tract epithelium, including upper airway disease and lower respiratory infection.
Follicular keratin plugging and dry skin; no common extra-cutaneous organ damage.
Inherited aminoacylase deficiency causes severe leukodystrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Feeding dysfunction and joint stiffness do not establish additional direct organ injury.
Epilepsy syndrome with absence, myoclonic and generalized tonic-clonic seizures; perioral movements are neurologic manifestations.
Factor IX deficiency; recurrent joint and muscle bleeding causes musculoskeletal damage in a substantial share (~30% or more). Intracranial bleeding is uncommon despite the HPO annotation.
Malignant soft-tissue tumor of skeletal muscle differentiation; no additional anatomical site is specified.
Reduced circulating platelet count; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes, and organ hemorrhage is not inherent across the umbrella.
Pontocerebellar and motor-neuron disease; hearing and visual impairment each 9/11, muscle atrophy 8/11. Respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular dysfunction rather than lung injury.
Disrupted electrical conduction within the cardiac atrium; any associated cardiomyopathy remains on the same axis.
Congenital skeletal malformation involving the number of phalanges in the great toe.
Neurodevelopmental disease, cataracts and renal defects define the syndrome; osteopenia occurs in 2/6 (~33%). Vascular findings in 1/3 omitted because of the cap.
Congenital ocular motor dysinnervation causes restrictive ophthalmoplegia, ptosis and extraocular muscle fibrosis/atrophy; these muscles are classified with the eye.
Mitochondrial complex I defect with metabolic acidosis; encephalopathy in 6/6 and dystonia in 5/5. Cardiomyopathy occurs in 1/6 (<30%); nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.
Turcot phenotype includes defining CNS tumors and colonic polyposis (9/18). Additional cancer susceptibility is not organ damage; cafe-au-lait pigmentation is non-damaging.
Plasmalogen biosynthesis defect usually manifests as RCDP2; skeletal dysplasia, cataracts and developmental impairment are characteristic, each affecting well over 30%.
Adenoma arising in the anterior pituitary endocrine gland; other organ damage is not inherent to this histologic category.
Site-variable histologic category predominantly represented by gastric and other gastrointestinal primaries; gallbladder and cervical origins are not shared across most cases.
Mass-forming tuberculous infection; the definition does not specify an organ, so cerebral or pulmonary localization cannot be assumed.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental impairment, brain abnormalities and frequent seizures; hypotonia and feeding difficulties do not establish separate muscle or gut damage.
